title: Fixture asserts a wall-clock backoff window: engram_source_root_selection_snapshot.rs:101 fails under concurrent test load
outcome: The source-root selection snapshot fixture proves that a retry backoff was applied after a transient capture failure, without asserting a wall-clock window that concurrent load can exceed. It passes deterministically under full-suite load.
acceptance: The assertion at src/tests/engram_source_root_selection_snapshot.rs:101 (and any sibling with the same pattern) checks the observable backoff, e.g. retry_at later than a timestamp taken before the install, instead of 'not yet due' within a 2.0-2.4 s window across a synchronous persistence step. No timeout is inflated, and no retry or skip is added.

Evidence that the original failure is a test timing defect and not a product regression: the discriminating runs Opus3 requested from Opus2, (A) master with the same 9 filters and (B) GREEN5 with only that module, are recorded with their run ids.
The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact landed input.

completion.summary: The snapshot fixture older_turn_in_retry (src/tests/engram_source_root_selection_snapshot.rs) no longer asserts that the retry is "not yet due" against the wall clock, which loaded hosts outran. It now records a timestamp before install_runtime_closing_result and asserts retry_at >= before_install + 1 s, proving a backoff was applied without a wall-clock window. No timeout was inflated and no retry or skip was added. It landed in the combined test-stability candidate (commit faf2de4f, master 65a11f06, pushed 22:21:08Z), whose FULL passed on DL560 (test-b14789ad: Rust 8054/0, vitest 5178/0). The independent acceptance evaluation passed all 3 criteria. The remaining Low (a scheduling stall of 1 s or more could mask a missing backoff) is filed as w-45f6775032b2.
